verdict.rationale: Sill reacts to a lagging link: the Mac detects held-back frames, warns on the device, and offers a quality the link can carry. It also starts remote sessions at a lower quality, and users can pick a Quality level on either device. However, the evidence shows a suggested change rather than continuous automatic adaptation, and a single Quality setting rather than separate resolution and frame-rate controls. Missing for 10: fully automatic in-session bitrate/quality adaptation, explicit user-settable resolution, explicit user-settable frame rate, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, quality adapts when the link falls behind, and I can set resolution and frame rate myself

citations.quote: Sill for Mac notices that it is holding frames back and tells your device, which says so over the picture and, in its Settings, offers a quality the link can carry.
Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry
Pick a lower Quality in the settings panel on your iPhone or iPad, or in the Sill menu on your Mac.
